We need to fix test code to compile. Issues: using JUnit 4 vs 5 mix. The imports from JUnit Jupiter (JUnit5) not available. Probably project uses JUnit 4. So replace JUnit5 annotations with JUnit4 equivalents: @Before, @After, @Test from org.junit. Remove @BeforeEach, @AfterEach, @DisplayName, @ExtendWith, MockitoExtension, @Mock. Instead use Mockito manually or simple stub. The test uses custom MockCostModel, not Mockito. So we can remove Mockito imports and annotations.

Also duplicate import of NaN. Also static import of NaN.NaN is wrong; NaN is a class with static field? In ta4j, NaN is a subclass of Num maybe with static instance NaN.NaN? Actually there is class org.ta4j.core.num.NaN extends Num with static final NaN NaN = new NaN(); So static import okay. But we have duplicate import.

Simplify: remove JUnit5 imports and annotations, use JUnit4 @Before, @After, @Test, maybe @Ignore for display names not needed. JUnit4 doesn't have @DisplayName; we can just keep comment.

Also need to import static org.junit.Assert.* for assertEquals, etc.

Also need to import org.junit.Before, org.junit.After, org.junit.Test.

Remove usage of reset(mockHoldingCostModel) which is Mockito reset; we have custom MockCostModel with reset method. So we can call mockHoldingCostModel.reset() directly. In @AfterEach we called reset(mockHoldingCostModel); replace with mockHoldingCostModel.reset().

But note that mockHoldingCostModel is declared as @Mock of type CostModel, but we actually want MockCostModel. In the test they later set up in @Before (JUnit4) to assign mockHoldingCostModel = new MockCostModel(); So we should change field type to MockCostModel rather than CostModel. Remove @Mock annotation.

Also need to adjust imports: remove org.mockito.* etc.

Also need to adjust usage of assertThrows which is JUnit5; JUnit4 has ExpectedException rule or try-catch. Could use assertThrows from JUnit4? Actually JUnit4 doesn't have assertThrows. Could use org.junit.Assert.assertThrows introduced in JUnit 4.13? Yes JUnit 4.13 added assertThrows method. So we can keep assertThrows static import from org.junit.Assert.*; it works.

But we need to import org.junit.Assert.* static.

Also need to import org.junit.Assert.assertSame etc.

Now fix errors about CostModel interface requiring equals method? The error says "does not override abstract method equals(CostModel) in CostModel". That suggests CostModel interface defines a method equals(CostModel). That's weird; maybe CostModel extends something? Actually maybe CostModel is a functional interface with method Num calculate(Position). But error indicates equals(CostModel). Could be they defined default equals? But compile error indicates it's abstract. So we need to implement equals method in MockCostModel and anonymous classes. However we can avoid by making MockCostModel extend an abstract class? But easiest: implement equals(CostModel other) method. Also need hashCode? Not required.

Let's inspect CostModel interface: likely has method Num calculate(Position), maybe also default equals? Not sure. But compile says abstract method equals(CostModel). So we need to implement equals(CostModel) in MockCostModel and anonymous inner classes. However we cannot modify anonymous inner classes easily; we can make them extend a helper class that implements CostModel with default equals implementation. Simpler: create a static abstract class AbstractCostModel implements CostModel { @Override public boolean equals(CostModel other){ return this == other; } } But equals signature expects equals(CostModel) not boolean? Actually equals method returns boolean. So implement.

But anonymous classes can extend AbstractCostModel to inherit equals implementation, but they currently implement CostModel directly. We can change them to "new AbstractCostModel() { @Override public Num calculate(Position position){...}}". That will compile.

Similarly MockCostModel should extend AbstractCostModel.

Also need to implement hashCode? Not required.

Now adjust imports: remove duplicate NaN import.

Also need to import java.lang.reflect.Field.

Now adjust test methods: they use assertEquals with message first param; JUnit4's assertEquals(String, expected, actual) works for objects. That's fine.

But they use assertEquals with expectedHoldingCost, actualHoldingCost (Num). Works.

Now they use assertSame, assertTrue, assertNull, assertThrows.
